What comes up in Kogarah

3 conditions, and each one is handled differently

Every site is scoped on the day. The table is what the work usually involves here rather than a statement about any particular property.

Walk up block near the centre

Three or four storeys of brick and concrete rather than a house, on a site with footpaths in use.

How it is handled
Survey, disconnections confirmed in writing, soft strip, then the structure in planned stages behind hoarding.
What does it
Mid to large excavator with a grapple, hoarding, dust control and traffic management.

Freestanding house going to dual occupancy

The other half of the work, where one set of services has to become two.

How it is handled
Disconnections confirmed, the dwelling and rear structures removed, then the block left level to the new set out.
What does it
Midi excavator with a grapple, sized to the side gap.

Freestanding houses

Single and double storey brick, brick veneer, fibro and timber. The era matters more than the material, because anything built before 1990 carries a hazardous materials assumption until it is tested.

How it is handled
Hazardous materials removed and cleared first, services disconnected in writing, then the structure taken down and the material separated as it falls.
What does it
Excavator with a demolition grapple, sized to the side access rather than to the house. Zero tail swing where the work runs hard against a boundary.

Kogarah

What shapes the work on these blocks

  • Mixed density in a small area A single knockdown and a walk up demolition can be neighbours, and they are not the same job.
  • Redevelopment pressure around the centre Which brings multi dwelling demolition and basement excavation.
  • Older housing stock Predominantly pre 1990, so a hazardous materials survey sits at the front of most scopes.
  • Narrow streets near the station Where traffic management frequently matters more than the structure does.

Kogarah ranges from quiet residential streets to busy frontages near the hospital and the station. Near the centre, truck standing is arranged rather than assumed and the working hours may be set by what is around the site.

Kogarah questions

What people ask before we start

Do you demolish unit blocks?
Yes. Walk ups and unit blocks are licensed work and they run as a planned sequence: a full hazardous materials survey, written confirmation of service disconnections, a soft strip, then the structure taken down in stages.
How long does a residential knockdown take?
Once the approvals and disconnections are in place, a straightforward single storey house is usually a matter of days. Asbestos removal and independent clearance come before that and are programmed separately.
How does a basement dig follow a demolition here?
Better as one contract than two. One contractor means the shoring, the batter and the truck movements are planned once, which matters on the tighter sites near the station precincts.
Who signs off that the asbestos is gone?
An independent licensed assessor, not the removalist and not us. Max holds demolition licence AD214737, the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists, and the clearance is arranged as part of the same job.
